title: Owner forms: minun, sinun, hänen, meidän, teidän, heidän
summary: Finnish uses an owner form called the genitive before a personal possessive noun. Learn the six owner forms from their basic pronouns.
objectives: Match my, your, his/her, our, and their to the six Finnish owner forms.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Finnish uses an owner form called the genitive before a personal possessive noun. Learn the six owner forms from their basic pronouns.

Minun means “my”, sinun “your” for one person, hänen “his/her”, meidän “our”, teidän “your” for a group, and heidän “their”. These are pronoun forms; the next lessons teach the noun endings. Hän does not identify gender.
The genitive owner pronoun comes before the supplied completed noun. Order the phrase without changing the supplied noun ending.
keyPoints: Owner forms: minun, sinun, hänen, meidän, teidän, heidän
Practise one singular possessed thing with the supporting forms shown.

steps: Minä (“I”) has the genitive owner form minun (“my”). Learn the pronoun form as a whole.
Sinä (“you”, one person) has the genitive owner form sinun. Use it for one owner addressed as “you”.
Hän (“he” or “she”) has the same genitive form hänen. Finnish does not choose a gender here.
Me (“we”) has the genitive owner form meidän. It names a group including the speaker.
Te (“you”, a group here) has the genitive form teidän. Keep it distinct from singular sinun.
He (“they”) has the genitive owner form heidän. It names several third-person owners, unlike hänen.
Put minun (“my”) before the complete shown word palloni (“my ball”).
Only pronoun selection and placement are taught here; keep the shown noun ending.
Choose sinun for one person addressed as “you”, then place it before pallosi (“your ball”).
The complete noun form is shown; its ending is taught next.
Choose meidän (“our”) for several owners including the speaker.
Place it before the shown pallomme (“our ball”); several owners can own one ball.
Choose teidän (“your”) for a group addressed as “you”.
Place it before the shown pallonne (“your ball”), keeping the supplied noun unchanged.

commonMistakes: Use genitive minun for “my”, rather than adessive minulla (“I as owner”). These forms serve different patterns.
Keep sinun (“your”, one person) distinct from teidän (“your”, a group).
Distinguish hänen (“his/her”) from heidän (“their”); Finnish does not use separate forms for his and her.
